title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Students must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and must have qualitative data they can analyze.

title: Quantitative Analysis for Planners
description: Introduces students to the basic statistical concepts used to address issues of public concern. Prepares students to perform, interpret, and evaluate quantitative data analyses commonly used in professional studies.

title: Analytical Methods for Planning
description: Emphasizes the development of analytical techniques proven useful in the fields of management and administration. Topics include multiple regression, cost-benefit analysis and discounting, decision trees, and other techniques useful for the purposes of community analysis and planning.

title: Statistics and Methods for Public Policy
description: Introductory course with focus on gaining a sound understanding of what constitutes credible evidence in support of policy arguments and management decisions.

title: Information and Public Policy
description: Evaluates strengths and weaknesses of qualitative and quantitative methods and the data used in making public policy claims. Looks at the bases of certain widely accepted measures of poverty, growth, environmental quality, and the like.

title: Qualitative Methods: Fieldwork and Data Collection
description: Covers fieldwork, data collections techniques, and related issues for anti-positivistic research. Data collection techniques include observation, physical traces, participation, in-depth interview. Data checks include veracity, detail, completeness, rigor.

title: Public Policy
description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst. Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.

title: Environmental Politics and Policy
description: Reviews and critiques literature on discussion topics including: the nature and effectiveness of environmental movements and policies; the role of science and technology; the use of economic incentives in policy; decentralization of decision making; and creating arenas for public involvement.

title: Qualitative Methods for Public Policy
description: Fieldwork, data collections techniques, and related issues for anti-positivistic research. Data collection techniques include observation, physical traces, participation, in-depth interview. Data checks include veracity, detail, completeness, rigor.

title: Economics of Government
description: Prepares students to analyze public policy questions with tools from economics. By the end, students should be able to identify important economic issues in public policy debates and consume and critique economic research on these topics.

title: Demographics for Planning and Policy
description: Provides planning and policy practitioners with a condensed, nonspecialist orientation to the sources, applications, and interpretation of population statistics, and conveys the steps used in constructing local-area population forecasts and projections.

title: Water Policy and Planning
description: Examines major issues in global water management including privatization, emerging water quality challenges, water system planning, affordability, conservation strategies, and flood resilience. Emphasizes integrated understanding of economics, governance, environmental health, technology, and development.

title: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Problem Solving in Planning
description: Explores the application of geographic information systems (GIS) in urban planning. Steps through a GIS-based planning procedure that balances housing, jobs, tax base, utilities, transportation, and the natural environment.

title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
description: Application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to the field of urban and regional planning. Emphasizes current issues that occur in actual implementation settings. Lecture/discussion followed by laboratory demonstrating the area of GIS discussed. Offers "hands-on" student usage of GIS software.

title: Urban Design Theories and Applications
description: Introduction to contemporary and traditional theories of urban design and their applications. Organized around one question: How might planning and design of built environment contribute to making a good city? National and international case studies are introduced.

title: Microeconomics and Public Policy
description: Introduces the fundamental principles of microeconomics that are required for applied policy analysis. Provides students with an intuitive understanding of the microeconomic approach, and familiarizes them with concepts used in applied public policy analysis.

title: Health Policy and Management
description: Multidisciplinary inquiry into theory and practice concerned with delivery, quantity, costs of health care for individuals and populations. Explores managerial and policy concerns regarding structure, process, outcomes of health services including the costs, financing, organization, outcomes, and accessibility of care.

title: Land-Use Policy
description: Examination of the role of public policy in guiding growth and development in urban and suburban environments. Description of a wide-ranging set of growth policies, the rationales underlying their use, controversies and legal constraints, and evaluation of their effectiveness.

title: Housing Policy
description: Examines theories and practices of housing policy and the relationship of housing to larger neighborhood, community, and regional development issues. Considers the roles of private for-profit and not-for-profit developers, lenders, and all levels of government in the provision of housing.
prerequisites_raw: Familiarity with basic statistics is required

title: Poverty and Development
description: Examines competing conceptualizations, methods of measurement, and poverty alleviation strategies widely used in developing countries. Focuses on poverty conceptualized as economic deprivation, well-being, vulnerability, and social exclusion.

title: Issues in Environmental Law and Policy
description: Treatment of legal and policy strategies for promoting environmental protection and deterring environmental degradation within the context of other societal objectives. Topical approach with a focus on problems of special interest to criminologists and to environmental policy specialists.

title: Foundations of Public Administration
description: Introduction to the complex and interdisciplinary field of public administration. Topics include theories of public organizations, the role of bureaucracy in the political process, leadership and accountability, and the changing nature of public administration.

title: Program Management and Evaluations
description: Introduces students to the principles and practice of program evaluation and management. Emphasis is on both the theoretical foundations and practical applications in a variety of decision-making contexts within the public and nonprofit sectors.

title: Public Budgeting and Financial Management
description: The practice and problems of modern fiscal management in government, including budgetary procedures, major expenditure and revenue sources, and public financing methods.

title: Sustainable Public Administration
description: Overview of administrative structures that guide effective responses to complex environmental management challenges. Explores important questions regarding who makes environmental decisions, the processes behind those decisions, and the influence of political and economic power on environmental management.

title: Designing and Consuming Research
description: In-depth examination of issues relevant to designing and evaluating research in public administration. Topics address ethical issues surrounding the responsible conduct of research, experimental, quasi-experimental, and case study designs, and reliability and validity of measurement.

title: Ethics and Leadership
description: The importance of ethical leadership and the many challenges to behaving ethically that leaders face in the public, private and non-profit sectors. Topics include diverse ethical theories and principles, theories of effective leadership, and approaches to fostering ethical behavior.

title: Policy and Ethics
description: Examines the challenge of identifying ethical principles that can guide us in formulating and assessing public policy, the public policy process from an ethical perspective, and the ethics of the individual engaged in the public policy arena.

title: Economic Democracy
description: Explores a wide range of radical democratic and egalitarian visions (including but not limited to the Marxist tradition) for a more sane, just, and sustainable future.

title: Public Finance for Urban Planning
description: Introduction to public project financing, including overviews of major expenditure and revenue sources, budgeting processes, and the relationship between budgeting and planning. Practical skills covered include public financing methods, relevant mathematical analytic techniques, and grant writing.

title: Site Development
description: Basics of site plan review (e.g., site/plot plans, floor plans, elevations) to ensure compliance with the zoning code, comparison of ministerial vs. discretionary review processes, Intersection of California Environmental Quality Act with review processes, understanding reporting requirements.

title: Global Urbanization
description: Examines the spread of cities worldwide in the 20th century. What are the political and economic causes of this process? What are the social-cultural, political, and economic effects? How is contemporary urbanization linked to global restructuring of other kinds?

title: MPP Capstone Research Project and Briefing
description: Focuses on an issue by emphasizing all aspects of the policy process, including problem definition, mobilizing support, design, implementation, management, and entrepreneurship. Two quarters in length. Students work in teams and present their product to faculty, students, and policymakers.

title: MPP Capstone Research Project and Briefing
description: Focuses on an issue by emphasizing all aspects of the policy process, including problem definition, mobilizing support, design, implementation, management, and entrepreneurship. Two quarters in length. Students work in teams and present their product to faculty, students, and policymakers.

title: Special Topics in Urban Planning
description: Special topics in urban and regional planning are offered from time to time, but not on a regular basis. Course content varies with interest of the instructor.

title: Planning for Sustainable Cities
description: Measurement, implementation, and evaluation of urban sustainability practices.

title: Site Planning and Design
description: Enhance understanding of planning documents, including site plans, sections, design guidelines that are part of the everyday practice of most planners. Students gain opportunities to create a physical end product that can be added to a professional portfolio.

title: Theories of Power and Empowerment
description: Studies different ways of thinking about power and its uses. Explores theories of power that inform various notions of empowerment, including resistance, participatory democracy, and workplace empowerment.

title: Transportation Practice
description: Broad survey of transportation policy issues that are confronting transportation planners, engineers, policymakers, and citizens.

title: Theoretical Approaches in Planning and Policy
description: Provides students with an overview of how theory is employed in urban planning and public policy research. Distinguishes between macro, meso and micro theories, including critical approaches. Cuts across disciplinary and topical boundaries. Ph.D. level course.

title: Urban Design Studio for Planners: An Introduction
description: Introductory urban design for planners. Organized around a variety of assignments to encourage learning by design in a studio setting. Students work on design projects and drawing assignments to learn practical aspects of urban design.

title: Collaborative Governance and Public Management
description: Introduction to inclusive management. To make effective use of public resources, public managers are inventing ways of managing that alter relationships within organizations, between organizations, between sectors, and with the public. Requires rethinking fundamentals such as leadership and motivation.

title: Environmental Theory and Topics
description: Provides an overview of various theoretical approaches to the study of natural and built environments. Cuts across disciplinary boundaries. Canonical studies of the environment and sustainability are examined. Ph.D. level course.

title: Urban Theory and Topics
description: An advanced course for Ph.D. students looking to study canonical and contemporary urban theory that is both interdisciplinary and global.

title: Professional Report
description: Workshop designed to assist M.U.R.P. students in conducting their professional reports. Students select topics, design projects, conduct professional investigations, and write up reports.

title: Planning Career Development
description: Introduces students to the career options for urban planners. Provides opportunities to meet with professional planners practicing in a variety of settings (public, private, non-profit) and introduces students to professional norms, roles, and career paths.

title: Urban Planning Practicum I
description: Engages students in practical planning projects in the community under a central theme within Planning. Students take a problem-solving approach and employ and further develop data gathering, analysis, graphic and oral communication, public engagement, and report writing skills.

title: Urban Planning Practicum II
description: Engages students in practical planning projects in the community under a central theme within Planning. Students take a problem-solving approach and employ and further develop data gathering, analysis, graphic and oral communication, public engagement, and report writing skills.
prerequisites_raw: PP&D 294A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
description: Dissertation research with Urban Planning and Public Policy faculty.

title: Research Design
description: Provides training in research design and methods. Students learn how to evaluate the strength of research findings based on the methods used by a researcher and learn to use lessons from the course to develop a research proposal.

title: Directed Studies in Urban Planning
description: Directed studies in Urban Planning.

title: Fundamentals of Vietnamese
description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Vietnamese. Natural approach with emphasis on four fundamental skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Conducted in Vietnamese.

title: Fundamentals of Vietnamese
description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Vietnamese. Natural approach with emphasis on four fundamental skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Conducted in Vietnamese.
prerequisites_raw: VIETMSE 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 1B is also accepted

title: Fundamentals of Vietnamese
description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Vietnamese. Natural approach with emphasis on four fundamental skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Conducted in Vietnamese.
prerequisites_raw: VIETMSE 1B with a minimum grade of C or VIETMSE S1AB with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 1C is also accepted

title: Intermediate Vietnamese
description: Designed for students to advance their Vietnamese language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Designed to develop writing and reading skills and communicative skills in authentic situations. Students are introduced to aspects of Vietnamese culture relating to lesson topics.
prerequisites_raw: VIETMSE 1C with a minimum grade of C and VIETMSE S1BC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 2A is also accepted

title: Intermediate Vietnamese
description: Designed for students to advance their Vietnamese language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Designed to develop writing and reading skills and communicative skills in authentic situations. Students are introduced to aspects of Vietnamese culture relating to lesson topics.
prerequisites_raw: VIETMSE 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 2B is also accepted

title: Intermediate Vietnamese
description: Designed for students to advance their Vietnamese language skills from introductory to intermediate level. Designed to develop writing and reading skills and communicative skills in authentic situations. Students are introduced to aspects of Vietnamese culture relating to lesson topics.
prerequisites_raw: VIETMSE 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into VIETMSE 2C is also accepted

title: Vietnamese Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. VIETMSE 10A is for language mentors.

title: Vietnamese Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. VIETMSE 10B is for language mentees.

title: Art History:Theories and Methods
description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in Art History.

title: Theoretical and Historiographical Research Methods
description: Provides students training in constructing and developing a research project integrating theoretical and historiographical methodologies.

title: Visual Studies: Theories and Methods
description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in Visual Studies.

title: Graduate Seminar in Visual Studies
description: Studies in selected areas of Visual Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading on a specific topic agreed upon by student and instructor.

title: Writing Practicum
description: Offered winter quarter each year and taught in a workshop format. Assists students with the preparation and revision of the dissertation prospectus so that they may advance to candidacy.
prerequisites_raw: VIS STD 290A and VIS STD 290B and VIS STD 290C

title: Reading for the Preliminary Examination
description: Directed reading in preparation for the preliminary examination. Formerly Visual Studies 298.

title: Prospectus Research
description: Research and writing of the dissertation prospectus.

title: Research in Anatomy
description: Individual research supervised by a particular faculty member.

title: Research in Anatomy and Neurobiology for First-Year Students
description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in the Department of Anatomy and Neurobiology for first-year Ph.D. students.

title: Human Gross Anatomy
description: Study and dissection of the human body, including muscular, skeletal, nervous, and cardiovascular systems. Emphasis on both normal and abnormal structure and function.

title: Human Neuroscience
description: Study of the human nervous system at the systems level including the physiology and anatomy of sensory, motor, and integrative functions.
prerequisites_raw: ANATOMY 202A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Human Microscopoic Anatomy
description: Lecture and laboratory course on human microscopic anatomy. Emphasis is on functional implications of structure of cells and tissues.

title: Human Microscopoic Anatomy
description: Lecture and laboratory course on human microscopic anatomy. Emphasis is on functional implications of structure of cells and tissues.
prerequisites_raw: ANATOMY 203A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Tutorial in Anatomy
description: Series of tutorials on advanced topics in anatomy.

title: Neuroanatomy from a Systems Perspective: Humans to Rodents
description: Covers structures and pathways of the functional systems of the human brain (motor, sensory, visual, auditory, and limbic) and how these are represented in rodents, emphasizing circuitry involved in learning and memory, neurodegenerative disorders, and neurotrauma.

title: Tutorial in Microanatomy
description: Special topics in microanatomy. Primarily library work, but study of prepared histological slides and photographs included.

title: Systems Neuroscience
description: Study of the mammalian nervous system at the systems level. Anatomy and physiology of sensory, motor, and integrative functions.

title: Epilepsy as a Window to Mechanisms of Neuronal Plasticity
description: Understanding the mechanisms of brain disorders provides novel insights into the normal function of neurons and circuits. Discusses approaches to studying mechanisms of brain function ranging from imaging, the use of models and others to study epilepsy.

title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
description: Focuses on critical reading, presentation, and discussion of current literature in neuroscience research.

title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
description: Focuses on critical reading, presentation, and discussion of current literature in neuroscience research.

title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
description: Focuses on critical reading, presentation, and discussion of current literature in neuroscience research.

title: Topics in Translational Neuroscience
description: One-hour seminar presentation by participating faculty or guest lecturer and open to the science community, followed by one-hour student discussion of the lecture topic or related topic. Students are responsible for presentations and readings.

title: Molecular, Cellular, & Developmental Neurobiology
description: Molecular aspects of the structure and function of neurons and glia including neurotransmission, synaptic modulation, and channels. Neural development at the cellular and molecular level including neurogenesis, pattern formation, trophic factors, axonal growth, and synaptic rearrangement.

title: Topics in Neural Circuit Mapping
description: Presentations/lectures by invited faculty and student discussion.

title: Scientific Communication
description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
description: First in a three-quarter foundation sequence introducing students to a broad range of contemporary art, media, and practices in relation to their 20th-century cultural and historical antecedents. ART 1A deals specifically with contemporary painting and photography.

title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
description: Deals with film/video/performance. Concerned with the development of modern/contemporary film, video, and performance, with a focus on experimental and avant-garde production from the early 20th century to today.

title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
description: Third in a three-quarter foundation sequence introducing students to a broad range of contemporary art, media, and practice in relation to their 20th-century cultural and historical antecedents. Deals specifically with space and cyberspace.

title: Changing Creativity
description: Explores creativity as a changing concept in historical and contemporary terms from the perspectives of producers, consumers, and institutions. Encompasses international perspectives and the role of new technologies in considering creativity as a resource for innovation and social change.

title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology
description: Examines creative activities in all spheres of life, including the "artistic" impulses that dwell in the individual. Culture is addressed in broad terms of the many institutions and cultural forces that shape everyday activities of listening, seeing, doing.

title: Visual Culture: A Culture Divided
description: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, controversies flourished in the mainstream media over purportedly obscene art, anti-American writing, and moral decay, among other issues. Examines these new conflicts as they manifest themselves in public life and everyday experience.

title: Visual Culture: Thematic Investigations
description: Considers a broad range of concerns and questions raised by various acts of appropriation in contemporary art and visual culture, such as originality, authenticity, authorship, translation, audience and aesthetics, temporal dimensions of a work, and context.

title: Visual Culture: Graffiti as Art and Language
description: Examines how graffiti art transforms urban landscapes and serves as a powerful means of global communication and cultural expression.

title: Topics in History of Contemporary Art
description: Surveys mid-19th and 20th-century art production, from modernity through post-modernity, in a historical and cultural context.

title: Art, Design, and Electronic Culture
description: Introduction to historical and theoretical foundations of digital media art, tracing how information technologies seeded growth of new expressive medium. Considers how today's pervasive digital culture evolved through interdisciplinary collaborations between artists, engineers, scientists, scholars.

title: Cultural History of the Anthropocene
description: A survey of the ongoing interactions between technological and social change through the 19th century and 20th century, with special attention to the history of computing, changing arts and cultural practices, and the idea of the Anthropocene.

title: Intelligences of Arts
description: Introduces contemporary neuroscience and new approaches to cognition – embodied, enactive, extended, situated, distributed. Reviews the history of related ethological, biological, psychological, technological, and philosophical traditions. Considers arts and cultural practices from these and other perspectives, and considers case studies.

title: Basic Drawing I
description: Encourages an investigation of the premises and limits of drawing, primarily, but not inevitably, as a two-dimensional medium. Includes slide presentations and discussions of the historical uses of a wide range of drawing. Materials Fee

title: Basic Painting I
description: Examination of the fundamental components of painting: color, form, space, surface, scale, and content. Studio work, slide presentations, and critiques of student work. Materials Fee

title: Basic Painting II
description: Further examinations of the essential qualities of painting: color, form, space, surface, scale, and content. Studio work, slide presentations, and critiques of student work. Materials Fee

title: Beginning Sculpture
description: The practice of sculpture in the contemporary arts; inclusion of spatial interventions, site-specific and environmental design, appropriation of found materials; techniques in cutting joining, and assembly of wood, metals, and plastics. May include casting, welding, and ceramics. Materials Fee

title: Matter and Media
description: A project-based introduction to tools and approaches for creating and sharing digital media content within internet-mediated social environments, with a particular emphasis on art-making and personal expression. Includes an overview of basic user experience and interaction design principles.

title: Interaction and Experience
description: An overview of digital video and audio production for the Web, emphasizing art-making and personal expression. Includes digital media aesthetics and conceptual design, basic audio and video recording, and fundamentals of desktop video, audio, and Web authoring software applications.

title: Basic Ceramic Sculpture
description: Exploration of use of clay as sculptural basis with an emphasis on development of an idea and its relation to contemporary and experimental art practice. Hand-building, glazing, finishing processes, and use of other structural materials. Materials Fee

title: Foundations in Media Design
description: Provides an overview of media design in the digital age, covering principles of design for different media (2D, time-based, interactive); history of relationship between art and design; and practice in working with different design approaches. Materials Fee

title: Foundations in Internet Art and Design
description: Introduction to creating art for the Internet, covering history and structure of networks; key types of net-based interactivity; basics of Web design and scripting. Materials Fee

title: Gizmology and Kinetics
description: Provides students with basic skills in materials, construction and design applicable to making machines, musical instruments and things with moving parts enabling work in kinetic sculpture, custom interactive systems, Mechatronics, Robotics, and Maker/DIY culture. Materials Fee

title: Introduction to Photography I
description: Introduction to technical underpinnings emphasizing photography as a contemporary art practice. Topics include 35mm non-automatic camera operation, exposure and lighting, black and white printing, introduction to digital photography, discussion of critical and historical issues. Materials Fee

title: Introduction to Photography II
description: Techniques covered include medium and large format cameras, digital photography, studio lighting, digital and analog color printing, mural room. Conceptual direction is developed through critiques, critical readings, discussions, slide lectures. Materials Fee

title: Beginning Video
description: Offers an introduction to the experimental histories and contemporary practices of video art with training in video, audio, lighting equipment, and editing software. Screenings, readings, and discussions engage issues of installation, representation, technology, and critical media literacy. Materials Fee

title: Basic Performance Art
description: Exploration of objects, gesture, action, text, image, and media to create narrative or non-narrative works. Elements of theory and history of performance art are discussed to illustrate techniques and styles to understand, identify, and articulate artistic vision and voice.

title: Special Topics in Basic Media
description: Basic instruction in media or disciplines not otherwise represented in the regular curriculum. Topics vary according to the instructor.

title: Special Topics in Art
description: Materials fee, topic dependent.

title: Artists as Writers
description: Contemporary art practice involves text, as final form or an integral element. Many contemporary artists consider writing as essential to their practice. Covers historical and contemporary uses of text and image as well as artists' writing.
prerequisites_raw: ART 9A and ART 11A . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Programming for Artists
description: Programming as a means to create interactive artworks with an emphasis on the integration of video, sound, text, and stills. Topics include basic concepts in programming, understanding the limits of code, working with video and audio files, and interface design. Materials Fee

title: Advanced Video
description: Students learn to conceive, develop, and produce original video works building directly upon previously learned skills. Use of video stage and post-production editing facilities. Lectures on video/film subjects, production strategies, readings, screening, field trips, and group critiques. Materials Fee

title: Performance and the Camera
description: Surveys the development of contemporary artists who use performance strategies in the making of videos and films. Students analyze the artist's conceptual approach to performative gestures, actions, and landscapes created for their video or film art.
prerequisites_raw: ART 1B or ART 81A or ART 91 or ART 128

title: How to be Clever with Stuff
description: How to Be Clever with Stuff is an introduction to the skilled embodied practices of arts and crafts, working with hand tools, wood, and steel. Class includes technical lecture/demos, short technical assignments, a self-initiated final project, and design drawing. Materials Fee

title: Afro-Futurism I
description: First of a two-part course on the futuristic artistic vision of Black film, video, and cyberspace. Deals with critical analyses of the Black image in Western Art history, and its association to contemporary Hip Hop culture, art, and music.
prerequisites_raw: ART 9A . Satisfactory completion of upper-division writing strongly recommended

title: Afro-Futurism II
description: Second of a two-part course on the futuristic artistic visions of Black film, video, and cyberspace. Deals with modern techno-culture, digital activism, and designing technology based on African aesthetic principles of contemporary Hip Hop International Culture.
prerequisites_raw: ART 9A . Satisfactory completion of upper-division writing strongly recommended

title: Issues in Media, Violence, and Fear
description: Violence has been instrumental in story-telling throughout history in art, literature, religion, and entertainment. Continuing presence of media violence provoked debates among parents, politicians, media producers, and academics. Examines history, theory, aesthetics, economics, and politics of violent representation.
prerequisites_raw: ART 9A . Satisfactory completion of the Upper-Division Writing requirement is recommended

title: Issues in Photography
description: Rigorous investigation of photographic practices and critical writings, the relationship of photography to the construction and maintenance of cultural institutions, the circulation of photographic ideas in society, and photography and technology.
prerequisites_raw: ART 1A or ART 71A or ART 71B or ART 152A or ART 152B or ART 152C or ART 152D or ART 152E or ART 190B . Recommended: Satisfactory completion of the Upper-Division Writing requirement

title: Issues in Techno-Arts
description: Addresses issues related to artmaking practices that emerge in tandem with new technologies. Topics include sociopolitical contexts of techno-art; utopic/dystopic framings; key moments in the history of techno-arts.

title: Issues in Experimental Film History
description: A critical study of experimental film/video art genres and production techniques considering their narrative, structural, iconographic, and cultural aspects. Hollywood narrative, Nouvelle Vague, American Independent, and Video Art compared in terms of production innovation, design, and conceptual content. Materials Fee

title: Issues in New Genres
description: Investigates issues in post-studio practices, including concepts of time, relational aesthetics, site-specificity, institutional critique, and the post-medium condition.
prerequisites_raw: ART 9A . Recommended: Satisfactory completion of the Upper-Division Writing requirement

title: Projects in New Technologies
description: Working with media such as electronic still cameras, desktop publishing, faxes, satellites, virtual reality, digitized imaging. Cultural issues pertinent to the emergence of new technology (e.g., ethical concerns, social impact, copyright laws, nontraditional approaches to distribution, cyberpunk, global markets).

title: Projects in Installation
description: Investigates interior installation in particular spaces. Working in teams, students install, discuss, and remove projects. Technical information and hands-on experience with various media is provided. Materials Fee

title: Place Making and Public Art
description: How do art interventions in public spaces inform our definition of "place" and develop culturally informed audiences? Students will engage in class projects and group investigations that question the traditional and institutional conceptual boundaries of exhibition/distribution.

title: Advanced Video: Installation
description: Students design and produce video installations including multi-channel and synchronized forms with an attention to space. Incorporates group and individual projects; lessons in projection, monitors, media players, editing; readings, screenings, and discussion. Materials Fee

title: Artist Books as Objects
description: Are artist books still relevant in the contemporary creative community? Focusing on intellectual content and raw physicality, students will explore this question and image/text relationships by creating handmade one-of-a-kind or edition book projects utilizing various mechanical reproduction techniques.
prerequisites_raw: ( ART 20A or ART 30A or ART 40 or ART 51 or ART 65A or ART 71A or ART 81A or ART 91 ) and ART 9A

title: The Artist Archives
description: Addresses ways in which artistic production and archival practice intermingle and overlap. Examines critical works on the nature of knowledge and the archive, and uncovers methodologies of knowledge production and how these inform what we think of as art.

title: Advanced Studio Topics--Painting
description: Provides an intensive and specialized working environment. Thematic issues and material strategies will be explored. Materials Fee

title: Advanced Drawing
description: Advanced studio problems in visual exploration. Students pursue individual solutions to self-defined and presubscribed projects. Techniques/materials are individual choice. Continual analysis of the personal process.

title: Advanced Figure Painting
description: Students develop technical skills in painting the figure. Live model sessions and projects that investigate the use of the figure in contemporary art.

title: Advanced Studio Topics--Sculpture
description: Provides an intensive and specialized working environment. Thematic issues and material strategies will be explored. Materials Fee

title: Advanced Studio Topics: Photography
description: Focused investigation of a range of issues in photographic practice, with an emphasis on developing individual student projects, refining critical thinking, and conceptual framing. Technical topics covered as required. Readings, lectures, critiques, labs. Materials Fee

title: Documentary Photography
description: Documentary practice is examined through the realization of photo-based projects. Thematic focus of student's choosing will be refined through lectures, discussion, technical demonstrations, field trips, labs, and individual meetings. Materials Fee

title: The Public Image
description: Strategies for artistic intervention in the public circulation of images are examined alongside the role images play in constructing public identity. Individual or collaborative student projects will be directed around course themes. Materials Fee

title: The Constructed Image
description: A studio investigation of theoretical ideas, critical possibilities, historical precedents, and various techniques involving the production of fabricated images. Techniques may include montage, digital, chemical and in-camera manipulations, studio constructions, appropriations, performance, and projected images. Materials Fee

title: Advanced Video: Projects
description: Focused on production of individually initiated projects in video, including narrative, experimental, documentary, and installation forms. Students create one substantial work or a series of shorter works through: pre-production, production, post-production; demos including editing, camera, and sound; weekly screenings, discussions. Materials Fee

title: Advanced Studio Topics: Performance
description: An intensive investigation of the practice of performance art, with an emphasis on the development of individual projects, and the refinement of various technical skills, as well as audiences, spaces, and cultural connections.

title: Advanced Studio Topics: Ceramic Sculpture
description: Discussion of ideas, techniques, and personal control of form. Clay body, fabrication, glazing, and firing. Emphasis on development of personal direction. Materials Fee

title: Advanced Projects
description: Students working in different mediums focus on ambitious research, planning, development, and experimentation, leading to a single work or focused series that is large in scope. The project is exhibited and documented at the end of the quarter. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ART 150 or ART 150C or ART 151 or ART 152A or ART 152B or ART 152C or ART 152D or ART 152E or ART 152F or ART 153 or ART 166A or ART 190 or ART 190B or ART 190C or ART 40

title: Critical Aesthetics
description: Surveys critical thought that has influenced twentieth-century art production, preparing the student to engage contemporary art with a critical eye, specifically addressing aesthetic and political debates of the historical avant-garde, the neo-avant garde, and postmodern culture.

title: Senior Project and Critique
description: Directed-study critique class in preparation for final project and life after graduation; documentation and portfolio preparation for graduate school. Investigation of exhibition spaces and funding opportunities, participation in artists' communities outside the university, and artists' rights issues.

title: Senior Projects and Critique in Photography
description: Directed group study focused on production of photographic projects of significant scope and ambition. Emphasis on preparation for continued study and/or practice in photography in advanced settings beyond the undergraduate university experience. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C and ART 71A and ART 71B

title: Art Internship
description: Under faculty supervision, students participate directly in a variety of art institution settings, including museums, galleries, and nonprofit organizations.

title: Honors Exhibition
description: Preparation, installation, and participation in the annual honors exhibition. Materials Fee

title: Independent Study
description: Individual study or directed creative projects as arranged with faculty member. Materials fee.

title: First-Year Graduate Seminar
description: Introductory theory class to contemporary art: intellectual history, theoretical antecedents, and current critical concerns.

title: Graduate Seminar Topics
description: In-depth discussion of contemporary art production in relation to a variety of theoretical, cultural, and historical topics. Material is determined by the given instructor's current research interest. Topics vary.

title: Graduate Seminar: Issues in Contemporary Art
description: Classroom interaction with artists, curators, critics, lecturers from fields outside of the arts or from cross-disciplines. Includes recommended readings, discussions, panel participation, writing assignments.
prerequisites_raw: ART 210 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Graduate Group Critique
description: Focus on studio production. Students are expected to help foster and develop an environment in which serious and sophisticated peer critique can take place.

title: Graduate Topics in Studio Production
description: Graduate group study of a specific medium or art practice (e.g., painting; video, installation, photography, sculpture/3D, performance, digital media, public art, sound art; film). Includes consideration of technical, theoretical, historical, and/or formal issues.

title: Interdisciplinary Projects
description: Intensive faculty-led discussion of in-progress graduate studio projects--can be discipline driven or working across fields in a rigorous interdisciplinary studio environment where students meet with the professor both individually and in small groups.

title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Independent study with a supervising faculty member to direct academic research, develop bibliographies, and discuss assigned readings.

title: Special Topics Seminar
description: Directed reading and/or study group on a given research topic. Agreed-upon meeting structure may be flexible in order to accommodate off-campus field trips and travel.

title: Graduate Thesis Writing Seminar
description: Seminar for writing as a component of the thesis. Different models of writing, text, and spoken word will be discussed. Required second year.
prerequisites_raw: ART 210 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 215 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 220 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Graduate Thesis Independent Study
description: Tutorials and directed study in thesis writing, research and/or studio production with thesis committee chair and/or thesis committee members to be taken during final quarters of study.
prerequisites_raw: ART 210 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 215 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 220 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Graduate Thesis, Exhibition Critique
description: Group critique required for matriculating M.F.A. students during the quarter in which their thesis exhibitions are scheduled. Public presentation/lecture on student's work required.
prerequisites_raw: ART 210 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 215 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 220 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 230 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 240 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 261 with a minimum grade of B- and ART 262 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Freshman Seminar
description: Weekly meetings consisting of presentations by faculty, professional staff, and Peer Academic Advisors provide information about the School of Biological Sciences, campus resources, learning skills, and special programs/opportunities.

title: Freshman Seminar
description: Faculty presentations and readings focused on the structure, function, opportunities, and current issues in the biological sciences.

title: EASE Seminar
description: Seminars designed to help students achieve success in STEM courses. Provides collaborative learning environment facilitated by undergraduate mentor. Students develop critical thinking and study skills. Also receive guidance to campus resources that assist acclimation to University.

title: Topics and Careers in Ecology and Evolution
description: Introduces students to topics, research opportunities, and career options in ecology and evolutionary biology.

title: Topics in Academic Success
description: There is an increasing awareness of the importance of non-academic factors (like belongingness) for student success. Provides students with peer mentoring and tools specific to different career stages that have been shown to improve student outcomes.

title: Career Decision-Making
description: An introductory course designed to facilitate the career decision-making process. Decision-making processes, values, and standardized tests of aptitudes, interests, and values are utilized with non-test data in appraising biological sciences career options.

title: Non-Health Sciences Career Exploration
description: A survey course designed to assist students in exploring non-health science career options. Lectures by professionals in various fields.

title: Introduction to Field Biology
description: Field excursions to introduce students to local field sites and resources.

title: Tropical Biology: Race to Save the Tropics
description: Population growth combines with tropical resource consumption by industrialized nations to cause high rates of deforestation, pollution, habitat fragmentation, and extinction of species. Discusses tropical biomes, their population, community, ecosystem processes, and possible means of conservation of biodiversity.

title: Evolution and the Modern World
description: Pandemics, disease, antibiotic resistance, your pets, the food you eat: evolution has shaped our world. Discusses the intellectual development of evolution and illustrates, with current events, that evolution is happening all around us, all the time.

title: Science of Cooking
description: The kitchen is used as a laboratory to introduce fundamental principles of biology, chemistry, and physics. A molecular/cellular analysis of cooking, including concepts such as protein structure, browning reactions, colloids, emulsions, carbohydrate metabolism, and development of flavor/texture through biochemical transformations.

title: Global Change Biology
description: Field trips and lectures that address ways in which humans are altering the global environment, with consequences for the ecology of animals, plants, and microbes.

title: Topics in Biological Sciences
description: Studies in selected areas of biological sciences.

title: California Teach 1: Introduction to Science and Mathematics Teaching
description: First in a series for students interested in becoming middle or high school teachers of mathematics or science. Students gain an understanding of effective, research-based teaching strategies. Includes supervised field experience in a K-12 classroom.

title: Evolutionary Psychology
description: Introductory overview of the field of evolutionary psychology. Surveys topics operating at the interface of social sciences, i.e. behavioral psychology and evolutionary biology, while developing select aspects of the history of this developing field.

title: Sustainable Landscaping: Design and Practices
description: Through lectures and hands-on work, students learn how to design habitats around dwellings, within cities, and in rural environments. These include traditional/sustainable landscaping, restoration, stormwater/wastewater treatment, xeriscaping, and low impact development design. Sustainable landscape plant materials emphasized.

title: Biology of Cancer
description: Biological, clinical, and psychosocial nature of cancer through the perspectives of medical researchers, biologists, physicians, and health educators. For students of all majors, designed so that each can increase personal awareness of the biology of cancer.

title: The Brain and Behavior
description: Introduction to how the brain works. Biological processes underlying perception, movement, sleep-wake cycles, motivation, language, learning, and memory. Changes in the brain associated with sex differences, drug use, aging, seasons, and time of day. Fundamental properties of the nervous system.

title: Drugs and the Brain
description: Introduction to the actions of drugs on the brain. How studying drug action helps reveal normal functions of neurons. How drugs can correct neural disorders or disrupt neural function. Biological issues related to drug abuse, drug addiction, and drug seeking.

title: Brain Dysfunction and Repair
description: Introduction to the disruptions in brain function that underlie disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinsonism, schizophrenia, and depression, and the basis for drug therapies. The brain's ability to repair itself after damage and the pros and cons of that repair.

title: Mind and Memory
description: Introduction to neural mechanisms underlying learning and memory. Emphasis on molecular changes that mediate memory as well as structures involved in different forms of memory. Additionally, examines the biology of memory phenomena, from extraordinary memory to false memory to amnesia.

title: Mood Disorders
description: There are significant differences in response to psychiatric illness across cultures. Delves into the neuroscience underlying mood disorder, investigating current pharmacological treatments and sociocultural influences on treatment outcomes.

title: AIDS Fundamentals
description: Considers the biological and sociological bases of the AIDS epidemic. Topics include the history of AIDS, current medical knowledge, transmission, risk reduction, and how the community can respond.

title: The Mind-Body Connection in the Neuroscience of Well-Being
description: Explores research that provides insight into how exercise, diet, sleep, contemplative practices such as mindfulness and meditation, and contemporary psychological therapeutic approaches alter brain function in beneficial ways to promote positive mental health well-being.

title: Introduction to Vaccines
description: Focus on introducing vaccines, covering how vaccines work, as well as how they are tested. Introduction to the immune system, to facilitate understanding how vaccines function. Also covers types of vaccines, clinical trials, and vaccine hesitancy.

title: Human Development
description: Processes leading to the birth of a healthy child and the avoidance of birth defects. Male and female reproductive systems, hormonal control of egg-sperm formations, sexual intercourse, contraception, venereal diseases, fertilization, cell division, embryonic development, fetal physiology.

title: Introduction to Biology Research
description: Students use the scientific method, ask and answer questions about environmental DNA, and develop professional skills applicable to any major or career. Focuses on the development of quantitative reasoning, science inquiry, and collaboration skills. Materials Fee

title: The Idiom and Practice of Science
description: The importance of biological sciences in our world is discussed. Topics may include brain and behavior, health and disease, genetics and society, and conservation biology. Primary goal is to encourage students to understand better the world in which they live.

title: From DNA to Organisms
description: Cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, and the biology of organ systems. Covers concepts of building blocks (nucleotides, amino acids, and cells) and of information flow (DNA to proteins, receptors to nuclei, the blood to distant organs, and DNA to offspring).

title: Honors From DNA to Organisms
description: Cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, and the biology or organ systems. Covers concepts of building blocks (nucleotides, amino acids, and cells) and of information flow (DNA to proteins, receptors to nuclei, the blood to distant organs, and DNA to offspring).

title: From Organisms to Ecosystems
description: Patterns of diversity, ecology, and evolutionary biology. Emphasis is on the Tree of Life and how its members are distributed and interact.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

title: Honors From Organisms to Ecosystems
description: Patterns of diversity, ecology, and evolutionary biology. Emphasis is on the Tree of Life and how its members are distributed and interact.

title: Genetics
description: Introduction to genetics. Basic features of replication and expression of DNA, cell division, and gene transmission. Recombination and mutation in diploid organisms.

title: Honors Genetics
description: Introduction to genetics. Basic features of replication and expression of DNA, cell division, and gene transmission. Recombination and mutation in diploid organisms.

title: Biochemistry
description: Structure and properties of proteins; major biochemical pathways and mechanisms for their control.
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97 ) and ( CHEM 1C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM M2C with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM H2C with a minimum grade of C-)

title: Molecular Biology
description: Biochemistry and replication of nucleic acids; molecular genetics; protein biosynthesis; genetic code; regulation of expression of genetic information; biochemical evolution.

title: Scientific Writing
description: Designed to give an overview of the basic aspects of scientific writing relevant to reporting research in the Biological Sciences.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 99 or BIO SCI 190 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: California Teach 2: Middle School Science and Mathematics Teaching
description: Second in a series for students interested in becoming middle or high school teachers of mathematics or science. Students gain an understanding of effective, research-based teaching strategies for grades 6-8. Includes supervised field experience in a middle school classroom.

title: Cell Biology
description: Analysis of the basic structure and function of animal cells, with an emphasis on the regulation of cellular processes. The basic features of membranes, cellular compartmentalization, protein trafficking, vesicular transport, cytoskeleton, adhesion, signal transduction, and cell cycle are covered.

title: Developmental Biology
description: Cellular and molecular analysis of how a fertilized egg develops into an organism consisting of complex structures such as the eye, arms, and brain. Emphasis is on the key concepts of developmental processes underlying pattern formation, growth, and regeneration.

title: Introduction to STEM Education Research
description: Introduces students to education research and topics studied in STEM education. Enables students to develop research questions, participate in research projects, design and utilize research tools, and contribute to STEM education research products.

title: Processes in Ecology and Evolution
description: An in-depth study of the mechanisms that drive evolution and ecology including: natural selection, mutation, genetic drift, speciation, extinction, life history patterns, population dynamics, ecosystem and community structure, predator-prey and host pathogen interactions, and social behavior.

title: Habitats and Organisms
description: Introduces students to local habitats and organisms through required field trips and applies ecological and evolutionary principles from BIO SCI E106 . Students also explore related literature.
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and BIO SCI E106 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Seminar in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
description: Invited speakers, graduate students, and faculty present current research in ecology and evolutionary biology.

title: Research Methods
description: Explores tools of inquiry for developing and implementing science research projects. Students undertake independent projects requiring data collection, analysis, and modeling, and the organization and presentation of results. Additional topics include ethical issues and role of scientific literature.

title: Human Physiology
description: Functional features of the major organ systems in the human body. Emphasis on homeostasis and the interactions of organ systems in health and disease. (Discussion of behavior and brain function deferred to BIO SCI N110 .)
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93 ) and ( CHEM 1C or CHEM M2C )

title: Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Consideration of the evolution of behavior, including ethological and psychological aspects and analysis of neuroanatomical, neurochemical, neurophysiological, and neuroendocrine systems underlying basic behavioral processes.

title: Developmental and Cell Biology Laboratory
description: Covers the division of cells, isolate cellular organelles (chloroplasts, mitochondria, nuclei), and follows changes in cells undergoing programmed cell death. Development is demonstrated in experiments showing cooperation of individual cells in forming a multicellular organism. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and ( BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104 )

title: Physiology Laboratory
description: Laboratory with a focus on the whole organism and its organ systems. Examples of structure-function relationships are drawn from both animal and human physiology. Cellular and molecular aspects are introduced as required. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and ( BIO SCI E109 or ( BME 120 and BME 121 ))

title: Microbiology and Immunology Seminar
description: Microbiology and Immunology majors attend weekly seminar on current microbiology and immunology research at UCI, career pathways, post-graduate programs, and other select topics.

title: Genetics Majors Seminar
description: Genetics majors attend a weekly seminar to discuss current research techniques and career opportunities in the field. Students have the opportunity to present their own independent research.

title: Neurobiology Laboratory
description: An in-depth exploration into biology and physiology of the nervous system. Labs include neuroanatomy, electrophysiology, pharmacology, behavior, experimental design, EEG, and scientific writing. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and ( BIO SCI N110 (may be taken concurrently) or BIO SCI N115A (may be taken concurrently))

title: Developmental and Cell Biology Majors Seminar
description: Developmental and Cell Biology majors attend a weekly seminar to discuss current research techniques and career opportunities in the field. Students have the opportunity to present their own independent research.

title: Advanced Biochemistry
description: Physical-chemical properties of macromolecules. Structure-function relationships in nucleic acids, protein, carbohydrates, and lipids. Integration and regulation of metabolism. Biochemistry of organs and biochemistry of diseases.

title: Biochemistry Laboratory
description: Properties of enzymes and the culture and isolation of mutants of microorganisms. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 99 and ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 )

title: Evolution Laboratory
description: Students perform experiments which illustrate important concepts in evolutionary biology such as natural selection, random genetic drift, inbreeding, age-specific selection, sexual selection, and phylogenetic reconstruction. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and BIO SCI E106 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Allied Health Microbiology
description: Introductory microbiology lecture and laboratory with an emphasis on microbial growth control and the relationship between microbes and human health.
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93 ) and CHEM 1C with a minimum grade of C-

title: Advanced Neurobiology I
description: In-depth coverage of neurobiology, ranging from molecular neurobiology to functional brain imaging. Discussion of molecular, cellular, and developmental neurobiology.

title: Advanced Neurobiology II
description: In-depth coverage of neurobiology, ranging from molecular neurobiology to functional brain imaging. Discussion of systems and behavioral neurobiology.

title: Advanced Molecular Biology
description: Mechanisms of gene expression; special emphasis on regulatory events that occur in Eukaryotic organisms other than initiation of transcription. Chromatin structure and rearrangement, RNA polymerases, cis- and trans-acting elements, RNA processing, transport and stability, protein synthesis, trafficking, and turnover.

title: Molecular Biology Laboratory
description: Students perform experiments which illustrate the chemical and biological properties of nucleic acids. Emphasis is placed on recent techniques in recombinant DNA technology including gene isolation and characterization. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 99 and ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 )

title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120 ) and BIO SCI E183 and BIO SCI E112L
